questions.q:
For a plane electromagnetic wave, the magnetic field at a point& $x$~and time~$t$~is :

$\overset{→}{B}\left(x, t\right) = \left[1 .2 \times {10}^{- 7}sin\left(0 .5 \times {10}^{3}x + 1 .5 \times {10}^{11}t\right)\overset{^}{k}\right]T$.

The instantaneous electric field~$\overset{→}{E}$~corresponding to~$\overset{→}{B}$& is :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
${E}_{0} = {B}_{0} \times C = 1 . 2 \times {10}^{- 7} \times 3 \times {10}^{8} = 36$

As the light is propagating in $x$ direction.

&~\left(\overset{^}{E} \times \overset{^}{B}\right) | | \overset{^}{C}$

$∴$~$\overset{→}{E}$ should be in $\overset{^}{j}$ direction.

So electric field $\overset{→}{E} = {E}_{0}sin\overset{→}{E} \cdot ( x, t ) = \left[- 36sin\left(0 . 5 \times {10}^{3}x + 1 . 5 \times {10}^{11}t\right)\overset{^}{j}\right]\dfrac{V}{m}$

$

questions.q: The electric field in a plane electromagnetic wave is given by,& $E = 50sin\left(500x - 10 \times {10}^{10}t\right)Vm^{- 1}$. The velocity of an electromagnetic wave in this medium is: (Given $c =$& the speed of light in vacuum).
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The equation of electric field is given in the question,& $E = 50sin\left(500x - 10 \times {10}^{10}t\right)Vm^{- 1}$~now compare it the equation of electric field in an electromagnetic wave,~$E = {E}_{0}sin\left(kx - \omegat\right)Vm^{- 1}$

$⇒ \omega = {10}^{10}rads^{- 1}$~and,~$k = 50m^{- 1}$, so the velocity of electromagnetic waves is,~$v = \dfrac{ω}{k} = \dfrac{1010}{50} = 2 \times {10}^{8} = \dfrac{2}{3}c$.

questions.q:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Electromagnetic waves carry energy as they travel through space and this energy is equally shared by the electric and magnetic fields.

Statement II: When electromagnetic waves strike a surface, a pressure is exerted on the surface.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Electromagnetic wave carries energy shared equally in magnetic and electric field which is given by, $= \dfrac{1}{2}{ε}_{0}E^{2} = \dfrac{B2}{2{μ}_{0}}$, as $E = cB$ and $c^{2} = \dfrac{1}{{μ}_{0}{ε}_{0}}$.

Also, Electromagnetic wave carries momentum and therefore exerts force when it strikes a surface.

questions.q:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I : Out of microwaves, infrared rays and ultraviolet rays, ultraviolet rays are the most effective for the emission of electrons from a metallic surface

Statement II : Above the threshold frequency, the maximum kinetic energy of photoelectrons is inversely proportional to the frequency of the incident light

In the light of above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below
options: Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Out of the three types of radiation, UV rays would be having highest frequency. The maximum kinetic energy is&

& ${K}_\max = hf - ϕ$

Clearly, the maximum kinetic energy is dependant on the frequency of the incident radiation and the work function of the metal.

From the given spectrums UV rays have the highest energy. Hence, this option is the correct one.

The associated magnetic field in Tesla is
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \overrightarrow{\mathrm{K}}=3 \hat{\mathrm{i}}+4 \hat{\mathrm{j}} \\ & \hat{\mathrm{K}}=\frac{3 \hat{\mathrm{i}}+4 \hat{\mathrm{j}}}{5} \\ & \hat{\mathrm{E}}=\frac{4 \hat{\mathrm{i}}-3 \hat{\mathrm{j}}}{5} \\ & \hat{\mathrm{~B}}=\hat{\mathrm{K}} \times \hat{\mathrm{E}} \\ & \hat{\mathrm{B}}=-\hat{\mathrm{Z}} \\ & \mathrm{B}_0=\frac{\mathrm{E}_0}{\mathrm{C}}=\frac{57}{3 \times 10^8}\end{aligned}$

questions.q:
Given below are two statements :

Statement I: A time varying electric field is a source of changing magnetic field and vice-versa. Thus a disturbance in electric or magnetic field creates EM waves.

Statement II: In a material medium, the EM wave travels with speed $v = \dfrac{1}{{μ}_{0}{ϵ}_{0}}$.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below.
options: Both statement I and statement II are true
Both statement I and statement II are false
Statement I is correct but statement II is false
Statement I is incorrect but statement II is true
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
According to the Maxwell’s EM theory, the EM waves propagation contains electric and magnetic field vibration in mutually perpendicular direction. Thus, the changing of electric field give rise to magnetic field.

Also, time varying magnetic field produces electric field. According to Faradays law, when magnetic flux changes in the region surrounded by conductor, it produces electric field (induced emf) in conductor.&

In a material medium& the EM wave travels with speed& given by& $\begin{cases}v & = \dfrac{1}{\muε} \\ v & = \dfrac{1}{{μ}_{0}{μ}_{r}( {ε}_{0}{ε}_{r} )}\end{cases}$

Thus, statement I is correct but statement II is false.

questions.q: Electromagnetic waves travel in a medium with speed of $1.5 \times 10^8 \mathrm{~m} \mathrm{~s}^{-1}$. The relative permeability of the medium is 2.0 . The relative permittivity will be:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & \frac{\varepsilon_{\mathrm{m}} \times \mu_{\mathrm{m}}}{\varepsilon_0 \times \mu_0}=\frac{\frac{1}{\mathrm{v}^2}}{\frac{1}{\mathrm{c}^2}} \\ & \varepsilon_{\mathrm{r}} \times \mu_{\mathrm{r}}=\frac{\mathrm{c}^2}{\mathrm{v}^2} \\ & \varepsilon_{\mathrm{r}} \times 2=\frac{\left(3 \times 10^8\right)^2}{\left(1.5 \times 10^8\right)^2} \\ & \varepsilon_{\mathrm{r}} \times 2=4 \\ & \varepsilon_{\mathrm{r}}=2\end{aligned}$

questions.q: A plane electromagnetic wave, has frequency of& $2 . 0 \times {10}^{10}Hz$~and its energy density is~$1 . 02 \times {10}^{- 8}Jm^{- 3}$~in vacuum. The amplitude of the magnetic field of the wave is close to~  \left(\dfrac{1}{4{πε}_{0}} = 9 \times {10}^{9}\dfrac{Nm2}{C2}\right)$~and speed of light~$= 3 \times {10}^{8}ms^{- 1}$.$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Energy& Denisty $= \dfrac{1}{2}\dfrac{B2}{\mu0}$

$B = \sqrt{2 \times {μ}_{0} \times \text{Energy density}}$

$B = \sqrt{2 \times 4\pi \times {10}^{- 7} \times 1 . 02 \times {10}^{- 8}} = 160 \times {10}^{- 9} = 160nT$

questions.q: An electromagnetic wave of intensity $50 \mathrm{Wm}^{-2}$ enters in a medium of refractive index 'n' without any loss. The ratio of the magnitudes of electric fields, and the ratio of the magnitudes of magnetic fields of the wave before and after entering into the medium are respectively, given by :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution: The speed of electromagnetic wave in free space is given by $\mathrm{C}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{\mu_{0} \epsilon_{0}}}$ In medium, $\mathbf{v}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{\mathrm{k} \in_{0} \mu_{0}}} \ldots$ (ii) Dividing equation (i) by(ii), we get $\therefore \frac{\mathrm{C}}{\mathrm{V}}=\sqrt{\mathrm{k}}=\mathrm{n}\frac{1}{2} \epsilon_{0} \mathrm{E}_{0}^{2} \mathrm{C}=$ intensity $=\frac{1}{2} \epsilon_{0} \mathrm{kE}^{2} \mathrm{v}\therefore \mathrm{E}_{0}^{2} \mathrm{C}=\mathrm{kE}^{2} \mathrm{v}\Rightarrow \frac{E_{0}^{2}}{E^{2}}=\frac{k V}{C}=\frac{n^{2}}{n} \Rightarrow \frac{E_{0}}{E}=\sqrt{n}$ similarly $\frac{\mathrm{B}_{0}^{2} \mathrm{C}}{2 \mu_{0}}=\frac{\mathrmB^{2} \mathrm{v}}{2 \mu_{0}} \Rightarrow \frac{\mathrm{B}_{0}}{\mathrm{~B}}=\frac{1}{\sqrt{\mathrm{n}}}$

questions.q: The oscillating magnetic field in a plane electromagnetic wave is given by ${B}_{y} = 5 \times {10}^{- 6}sin1000\pi\left(5x - 4 \times {10}^{8}t\right)T$. The amplitude of electric field will be
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given here,& ${B}_{y} = 5 \times {10}^{- 6}sin1000\pi\left(5x - 4 \times {10}^{8}t\right)T$

Here, peak value of magnetic~field,~${B}_{0} = 5 \times {10}^{- 6}T$

Now the speed of the wave~$v = \dfrac{ω}{k} = \dfrac{1000\pi \times 4 \times {10}^{8}}{1000\pi \times 5} = 8 \times {10}^{7}ms^{- 1}$

Using relation between magnetic and electric field,~

Peak value of electric~field is~${E}_{0} = {B}_{0}v = 5 \times {10}^{- 6} \times 8 \times {10}^{7} = 4 \times {10}^{2}Vm^{- 1}$

questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R

Assertion A : EM waves used for optical communication have longer wavelengths than that& of microwave, employed in Radar technology.

Reason R : Infrared EM waves are more energetic than microwaves, (used in Radar)

In the light of given statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below.
options: Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is false but R is true
A is true but R is false
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
An& optical& telecommunication& is& communication& at a distance using light to carry information. It can be performed visually or by using electronic devices.

The wavelength of the microwaves are greater than that of the common optical light waves.

Hence, the Assertion is not correct. But, because of the small wavelength, the electromagnetic waves are more energetic than the microwaves. Hence, the reason is true.

questions.q: A plane electromagnetic wave of frequency $25GHz$ is propagating in vacuum along the z-direction. At a particular point in space and time, the magnetic filed is given by $\overset{→}{B} = 5 \times {10}^{- 8}\overset{^}{j}T .$ The corresponding electric field $\overset{→}{E}$ is (speed of light $= 3 \times {10}^{8}ms^{- 1}$ )
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given, the electromagnetic wave is propagating in& $z$~i.e.,~$+ \overset{^}{k}$~direction.

The relation between the magnitudes of electric field, magnetic field and the speed of light is given by

\left|E\right|\left|B\right| = C$

$⇒ \left|E\right| = \left|B\right| \times C$
$⇒ \left|E\right| = 5 \times {10}^{- 8} \times 3 \times {10}^{8} = 15Vm^{- 1}$

We know that the direction of propagation of electromagnetic wave is along~$\overset{→}{E} \times \overset{→}{B}$.

So,~$\overset{→}{E} = 15\overset{^}{i}Vm^{- 1}$

$

questions.q: The electromagnetic waves travel in a medium at a speed of $2 . 0 \times {10}^{8}ms^{- 1}$. The relative permeability of the medium is $1 . 0$. The relative permittivity of the medium will be
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Here, $v = 2 \times {10}^{8}\text{m}s^{- 1}$ and ${μ}_{r} = 1$

The speed of electromagnetic waves in a medium is given by~$v = \dfrac{1}{\muε} . .. \left(i\right)$

where $\mu$ and $ε$ are absolute permeability and absolute permittivity of the medium.
Now, $\mu = {μ}_{0}{μ}_{r}$ and $ε = {ε}_{0}{ε}_{r}$
Then, we have,~

$v = $\dfrac{1}{{μ}_{0}{μ}_{r} \times {ε}_{0}{ε}_{r}} = \dfrac{1}{{μ}_{0}{ε}_{0}} \times \dfrac{1}{{μ}_{r}{ε}_{r}} = \dfrac{c}{{μ}_{r}{ε}_{r}}

$or{ε}_{r} = $\dfrac{c2}{v^{2}{μ}_{r}} = \dfrac{\left(3 \times {10}^{8}\right)2}{\left(2 \times {10}^{8}\right)2} = \dfrac{9}{4} =$2 . 25$

questions.q:
The electric field and magnetic field components of an electromagnetic wave going through vacuum is described by

& ${E}_{x} = {E}_{0}sin \left(kz - \omegat\right)$

${B}_{y} = {B}_{0}sin \left(kz - \omegat\right)$

Then the~correct relation between~${E}_{0}$~and~${B}_{0}$& is given by&
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
As we know, electric field and magnetic field are related as&

${E}_{0} = c{B}_{0}$, where,~$c$~is speed of light in vacuum

$\text{Also}c = \dfrac{ω}{k}$

$⇒ {E}_{0} = \dfrac{ω}{k}{B}_{0}$

$⇒ {E}_{0}k = \omega{B}_{0}$

(Use ${ϵ}_{0} = 8 . 85 \times {10}^{- 12}C^{2}N^{- 1}m^{- 2}$)

The formula to calculate the intensity of the electromagnetic wave is given by

From equation (1), it follows that

$

questions.q: The electric field of a plane polarized electromagnetic wave in free space at time& $t = 0$ is given by the expression $\overset{→}{E}  \left(x, y\right) = 10\overset{^}{j}cos \left($6x + 8z\right)$. The magnetic field $\overset{→}{B}  \left(x, z, t\right)$ is given by ($c$ is the velocity of light.)$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$E = {E}_{0}cos \left(\omegat - \overset{→}{K} \cdot \overset{→}{r}\right)

$∴$ At any time~$t$,

$\overset{→}{K} = 6\overset{^}{i} + 8\overset{^}{k}$

${B}_{0} = $\dfrac{{E}_{0}}{c} = \dfrac{10}{c}

$\lambda = $\dfrac{2\pi}{k} = \dfrac{2\pi}{10} = \dfrac{π}{5}

Also, $\overset{→}{E} $\times \overset{→}{B} = \overset{→}{c}

$∴ $\omega =$2\pif = $\dfrac{2\pic}{λ}

\left|\begin{cases}\overset{^}{i}$& \overset{^}{j} & \overset{^}{k} \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ {B}_{x} & {B}_{y} & {B}_{z}\end{cases}\right| = $\dfrac{6\overset{^}{i} + 8\overset{^}{k}}{10}

\omega =$2$\pi \times$c\left(\dfrac{π}{5}\right) =$10c$

$∴ \overset{^}{i}\left[{B}_{z} -$0\right] + \overset{^}{j}\left($0\right) + \overset{^}{k}\left(- {B}_{x}\right) =$0.6\overset{^}{i} - 0.8\overset{^}{k}$

Comparing the coefficients on both sides,

$∴ {B}_{z} = 0.6; {B}_{x} = - 0.8$

\left|\overset{→}{B0}\right| = \dfrac{10}{c}\left(-$0.8\overset{^}{i} + 0.6\overset{^}{k}\right) = $\dfrac{- 8\overset{^}{i} + 6\overset{^}{k}}{c}

So the magnetic field,$\overset{→}{B} = $\dfrac{1}{c}\left(-$8\overset{^}{i} + 6\overset{^}{k}\right)cos ⁡ \left($6x + 8z - 10ct\right)tesla$

questions.q: Light wave travelling in air along $x$-direction is given by ${E}_{y} = 540sin\pi \times {10}^{4}\left(x - ct\right)Vm^{- 1}$. Then, the peak value of magnetic field of wave will be (Given $c = 3 \times {10}^{8}ms^{- 1}$)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given here,& ${E}_{y} = 540sin\pi \times {10}^{4}\left(x - ct\right)Vm^{- 1}$

Here, peak value of electric field,~${E}_{0} = 540Vm^{- 1}$

Using relation between magnetic and electric field,~

Peak value of magnetic field is~${B}_{0} = \dfrac{E0}{c} = \dfrac{540}{3 \times {10}^{8}} = 18 \times {10}^{- 7}T$

questions.q: The energy density associated with electric field& $\overset{→}{E}$~and magnetic field~$\overset{→}{B}$~of an electromagnetic wave in free space is given by (${ε}_{0} -$~permittivity of free space, ${μ}_{0} -$& permeability of free space)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
When an electromagnetic wave propagates from the source, it transfers energy to the objects in its path.& Electric and magnetic fields serve as energy reservoirs for electromagnetic waves. An electromagnetic wave contains the same amount of energy as are contained in the electric and magnetic fields together. In such situation, the energy density of the electromagnetic wave is equal to the sum of the energies of the electric and magnetic fields.

The average electric and magnetic energy densities are given by

$\begin{cases}{U}_{E} & = & \dfrac{1}{2}{ε}_{0}E^{2} \\ {U}_{B} & = & \dfrac{1}{2}\dfrac{B2}{\mu0}\end{cases}$
